subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override a later stricter operator/global exec policy when a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source and tests treat persisted session exec fields as intended defaults, but the reported behavior can weaken a later operator security change and therefore needs an explicit security-boundary decision.

options.title: Make global policy the upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they would exceed current global or agent exec security policy, with focused reset or migration coverage.

options.title: Keep persisted session overrides
options.body: Preserve current behavior and document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make global policy the upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields when they would exceed current global or agent exec security policy, with focused reset or migration coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the `/exec` session override feature and focused resolver coverage points to this owner path.
